solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

blocks.note: surface reading: a woman called Donna who is moody or unreliable from time to time
setter's reading: read the name taking alternate letters, switching between keeping and dropping each one, and its even letters spell a little word

explanation.walkthrough: Taking every other letter of DONNA gives ON, so the name works intermittently; the answer is the phrase for that alternating pattern.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase describes something happening intermittently, at intervals rather than continuously, which is what periodically means.

indicators.note: to cross something is to go over and across it, so one piece straddles another

blocks.note: O is the standard abbreviation for old
cans are vessels for holding liquid
E is the abbreviation for eastern

explanation.surface: Ancient ships sailing across the waters of the East.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old vessels' suggests galleons, but the vessels are humble cans, with the eastern E slipped inside them.
explanation.definitionFit: Oceans are the great seas of the world, so the plural noun fits a general word for bodies of water.

clue.text: Hope adult is on top of steeple

indicators.note: in a down clue the upper piece sits above the next, so being on top means coming first

blocks.note: A is the film-rating abbreviation for adult
the tapering pointed structure on a church tower, the defining part of a steeple

explanation.surface: A grown-up perched on a church steeple, hoping for the best.
explanation.walkthrough: This is a down clue, so A placed on top of SPIRE simply comes before it.
explanation.definitionFit: To aspire is to long or wish for something ambitious, so the verb works as a synonym for hope.

indicators.note: finally points to the end of a word, so only its closing letter is kept

blocks.note: the last letter of lobbed
a rake is a toothed garden tool

explanation.surface: Someone throws a garden tool and shouts a warning to take cover.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Duck!' reads as a shouted warning, but it is the noun for the bird.
explanation.definitionFit: A drake is a male duck, so the answer is a specific example of the bird named.

clue.text: Formation of masts, sails, etc in large European ship

indicators.note: something in another is placed within it, so one piece sits inside a second

blocks.note: a ship's rig is the arrangement of its masts and sails
fat means large or bulky
E is the abbreviation for European

explanation.surface: A description of the rigging aboard a big European sailing vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Formation of masts, sails, etc' reads as part of the ship's description, but it is wordplay for the ship's rigging, set inside the word for large.
explanation.definitionFit: A frigate is a type of warship, historically a fast sailing vessel, so it is an example of a ship.

clue.text: Sunglasses husband exchanged for shop’s last suit

indicators.note: one thing exchanged for another is swapped out and replaced
the last of a word is its final letter, the only one kept

blocks.note: shades is an informal word for sunglasses
H is the abbreviation for husband
the final letter of shop

explanation.surface: Swapping sunglasses at a shop to find something that suits.
explanation.walkthrough: In SHADES the H is replaced by P, giving SPADES. 'Suit' looks like clothing or a verb but is the card suit.
explanation.definitionFit: Spades is one of the four suits in a pack of playing cards, alongside hearts, diamonds and clubs.

indicators.note: what we are told reaches us by ear, so the word is judged by its sound

blocks.note: a principle is a fundamental rule

explanation.surface: Someone announcing the key rule everyone has been given.
explanation.walkthrough: PRINCIPLE (a rule) and PRINCIPAL (chief) are pronounced identically, a pair often confused in writing.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective principal means first in rank or chief, so it serves for most important.

clue.text: Find out record with six balls?

blocks.note: a disc is a gramophone record
in cricket an over is a set of six balls bowled from one end

explanation.surface: Learning about a record set in an innings with six deliveries.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, a bowler delivers six balls in an over, so the question mark flags that cricket definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To discover is to learn or come upon a fact for the first time, the same as finding something out.

indicators.note: to surround is to enclose on all sides, so one piece goes around others

blocks.note: a sense is a feeling or perception
US abbreviates the United States, hence American
P is the symbol for pressure in physics

explanation.surface: Someone sensing pressure coming from America and growing anxious.
explanation.walkthrough: P is the physics symbol for pressure; 'Feeling' looks like the definition but is the outer word.
explanation.definitionFit: Suspense is the anxious uncertainty of waiting for an outcome, close in meaning to nervous unease.

indicators.note: made different, the letters end up in a changed order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A dieter with the same hip measurement but a different reading on the scales.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Weight' reads as body weight in the dieting picture, but it means stress or importance.
explanation.definitionFit: Giving weight to something means stressing its importance, which is exactly what emphasis is.

blocks.note: first meaning: escapes or steers clear of
second meaning: plural of the old word for a young unmarried woman

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as someone shy keeping away from girls; the two words are separate meanings of one word.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means fails to meet or dodges; as a plural noun it is an old term for young women.

indicators.note: somewhat means to some extent, so only part of the following letters is used

blocks.note: letters running across the two words

explanation.surface: A rather shy boss is not getting anything done.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer sits across the join in tIMID LEader.
explanation.definitionFit: Idle describes a person or machine that is inactive, doing nothing, exactly as not working implies.

indicators.note: about here means around, so one piece goes round another

blocks.note: a sister is a senior nurse in a British hospital
mad means angry
I is the symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: A sibling cross about the latest childminder.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a sister is a senior ward nurse, not just a sibling. I is the physics symbol for electric current.
explanation.definitionFit: A nursemaid is a woman employed to look after children, which is what a nanny does.

blocks.note: C is the abbreviation for Conservative
hose are stockings or tights, worn as undergarments

explanation.surface: Sensible, modest underwear has been picked out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Conservative' looks like an adjective for the underwear; it is just the party abbreviation C.
explanation.definitionFit: Chose is the past tense of choose, so it means picked or selected, matching the past participle in sense.

clue.text: Long leg he ignored at first

indicators.note: ignoring the start of a word means its opening letter is left out

blocks.note: pins is slang for legs
the pronoun without its first letter

explanation.surface: A man with a lengthy limb that he overlooked at the start.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Long' looks like an adjective describing the leg, but it is a verb meaning yearn.
explanation.definitionFit: To pine for something is to yearn or ache for it, the verb sense of long.

clue.text: One masculine person requiring medical care is aching

blocks.note: I is the Roman numeral one
M is the abbreviation for masculine
a patient is someone receiving medical treatment

explanation.surface: A man in need of medical attention is in pain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Aching' suggests physical pain in the hospital picture, but it means longing eagerly.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone aching to do something is restlessly eager for it, which is to be impatient.

blocks.note: ex means former or old
to press clothes is to smooth them with an iron

explanation.surface: Describing a vintage locomotive that runs smoothly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old, smooth' looks like a pair of adjectives for the train; both are wordplay, the second a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: An express is a fast train making few stops, so it is one particular kind of passenger service.

indicators.note: to doctor something is to tamper with it, so the letters are altered

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A physician welcomes us with a wave of the hand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor' reads as a person greeting us, but it is a verb meaning tamper with.
explanation.definitionFit: Gestures are movements of the hands or body that convey meaning, so they are nonverbal signals.

clue.text: Exact chapter covered by a member of the clergy

indicators.note: whatever is covered has something over it on both sides, so it sits within

blocks.note: C is the abbreviation for chapter
taken as written
a curate is an assistant to a parish priest

explanation.surface: A clergyman takes charge of a precise section of scripture.
explanation.walkthrough: C goes inside A CURATE, just after the A: A(C)CURATE.
explanation.definitionFit: Accurate means correct in every detail, free of error, which is what exact describes.

clue.text: Gets free pies with 50 per cent off wraps

indicators.note: removing half of a word leaves only its other half to use

blocks.note: the second half of the word, the first two letters dropped
capes are sleeveless cloaks or wraps

explanation.surface: A bakery offer: free pies with half price off wraps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gets free pies' reads like a deal, but 'Gets free' is the definition; 'wraps' are garments, not tortilla wraps.
explanation.definitionFit: To escape is to break loose from confinement, so escapes is the present-tense verb for gets free.

blocks.note: first meaning: slang for jail
second meaning: a fuss or disturbance

explanation.walkthrough: It reads like a riot in a jail; the two words are separate meanings of one short word.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is informal slang for jail, and also means an excited fuss, as in causing a stir.

indicators.note: placed in another thing means set inside it

blocks.note: L is the abbreviation for left
a cot is a small bed

explanation.surface: A naive young man is left lying in bed.
explanation.walkthrough: L goes inside COT. In British sport a colt is a young, inexperienced player, extending the horse sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A colt is a young male horse, and by extension a novice or untried young person.

clue.text: Brownies perhaps arrived – treats regularly disposed of

indicators.note: throwing away letters at regular intervals leaves only every other one

blocks.note: came means arrived
the second, fourth and sixth letters of the word

explanation.surface: Chocolate brownies turn up and the treats are eaten one after another.
explanation.walkthrough: The Brownie was a cheap, popular Kodak box camera; 'perhaps' marks it as an example. 'Brownies' suggests cakes or young Guides.
explanation.definitionFit: Kodak Brownies were simple box cameras, so the plural is an example of the category of photographic devices.

clue.text: Battle wound? This might take away the pain

definitions.text: This might take away the pain

indicators.note: wound as the past of wind means twisted round, so the letters are coiled into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A soldier with an injury from combat needs something for the pain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Battle wound' reads as an injury, but 'wound' rhymes with sound and means twisted.
explanation.definitionFit: A tablet is a pill, such as a painkiller, which a patient swallows to relieve aches.

indicators.note: to keep something is to hold it, so one piece holds another

blocks.note: a CD is a compact disc, one example of a recording
to ease is to calm or soothe

explanation.surface: Someone halted a recording session while staying composed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stopped recording' reads as one phrase, but 'Stopped' alone is the definition and 'recording, possibly' is CD.
explanation.definitionFit: Ceased is the past tense of cease, meaning came to an end or halted, just like stopped.

blocks.note: Tango is T in the NATO phonetic alphabet
an aunt is a female relative

explanation.surface: A man dancing a tango with his aunt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Guy' looks like a man's name, but as a verb it means to mock; the 's stands for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: To guy someone is to ridicule or make fun of them, the same as to taunt them with jeers.

clue.text: Swift interpretation misinterpreted initially by referee

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so each word gives only its opening letter

blocks.note: the first letters of the two words
to referee a dispute is to mediate in it

explanation.surface: A quick reading of something a referee got wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: 'referee' looks like a noun for the official, but it is the verb meaning to arbitrate.
explanation.definitionFit: Immediate means happening at once without delay, so it is a synonym for prompt or quick.

clue.text: Day on the river, under the weather – this could be boring

blocks.note: D is the abbreviation for day
R is the abbreviation for river
under the weather means unwell

explanation.surface: A day out on the river while feeling poorly sounds tedious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boring' seems to mean dull, but here it means making holes.
explanation.definitionFit: A drill is a tool used for boring holes, so it is the thing doing the boring in that sense.

blocks.note: re means concerning or about
A is the abbreviation for answer
a Red is a socialist or communist

explanation.surface: Someone brought up a matter about a reply to a left-winger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Raised concerning' reads as raising a concern, but 'Raised' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To rear children or animals is to bring them up, and raised has the same sense.

clue.text: Anthea potentially has three of these newspaper pieces

definitions.text: Anthea potentially has three of these

blocks.clueFragment: Anthea potentially has three of these
blocks.note: first meaning: the grammatical words a, an and the, which can be split out of the name
second meaning: written items in a newspaper

explanation.walkthrough: ANTHEA can be split as AN + THE + A, three grammatical articles; 'potentially' admits the name only contains them if read that way.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both the grammar words a, an and the, and individual written reports in a paper.

clue.text: Essentially remonstrate about hospital department’s smells

indicators.note: the essence of something is its core, so only the central letter is kept

blocks.note: the middle letter of the eleven
C abbreviates circa, Latin for about
ENT is the ear, nose and throat department, plus the 's

explanation.surface: Someone basically complains about the odours in a hospital ward.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' looks like a link to the complaint, but it is C for circa.
explanation.definitionFit: Scents are odours or fragrances, so the plural noun matches the noun sense of smells.

indicators.note: done strangely means done in an odd way, so the letters come out in an unusual order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Something oddly found only among women.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unique to ladies' reads as exclusive to women, but 'Unique' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An isolated case is a single, one-off instance with no parallel, the sense in which unique is meant.
